picks.file: Tipus civitatis Lubline(n)sis in regno Poloniae (...) - btv1b53235785m (2 of 3).jpg
picks.what: Engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 6
picks.why: true profile view with the castle, churches and town gates labeled; clean scan with no fold; legend panel trimmed

picks.file: Widok Lublina od strony południowej J. Maszewski 1774.jpg
picks.what: View of the town from the south
picks.why: detailed view of the walled Old Town and its churches; ornamental frame, sun rays and lower figures trimmed

picks.what: View from the castle over the Old Town, photograph (National Library of Poland)
picks.why: Dominican church, Trinitarian Tower and cathedral towers above the castle hill; black border trimmed

picks.file: Panorama of Lublin from the observation deck.jpg
picks.what: View from the castle keep over the Old Town
picks.why: same landmarks as the Bułhak view, in color; shutter, railing and deck trimmed off

gaps: P0: no candidates. P2: only #5 (1677, a schematic town under a large empty cartouche, doubtful as a true view) and #4 (small undated copy of the Braun and Hogenberg view, 1650–1749). P4: #9 (‘after 1850’, magazine woodcut) and #10 (‘19th century’ lithograph) have no usable date.
notes: #2 is the Braun and Hogenberg vol. 6 plate (BnF copy dated 1635), dated to first publication 1617; #3 is the same plate colored but with a dark fold line through the cathedral, and #1 is photographed in the open book. #12’s record says only ‘before 1930’ (printed 1934); Commons files it under Lublin in the 1920s, hence ‘1920s’. #16 (2025 night view of an Old Town street with the Trinitarian Tower, Krzysztof Popławski) is a strong P6 alternative if the trimmed #15 strip is too narrow.
